pageCache.text:
A warm welcome to Green Oaks Federation
On behalf of the Green Oaks Federation, I would like to extend a warm welcome to you and your family. The Green Oaks Federation consists of Oakwood Infant and Greenfields Junior School, which both sit within the village community of Hartley Wintney.
The two schools share the same vision and values for education. Our dedicated team work in collaboration to ensure all of our children are nurtured to grow into happy, responsible and respected members of our community.
This website is designed to give you information about Oakwood Infant and Greenfields Junior School and give you an insight into the work that we do across our Federation. If you have any further questions please contact either school and we will be pleased to help.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Green Oaks Federation - Early Years Foundation Stage
pageCache.text:
Early Years
Foundation Stage
We believe every child is unique and curious, learning best through positive relationships and inspiring environments. Our curriculum builds strong foundations across the seven areas of learning within Early Years Foundation Stage curriculum.
Through a balance of child led play and focused teaching, we help children become confident, independent learners. We work closely with families to support each child’s journey, from their first days in Reception to being ready for Key Stage 1.
Starting at Oakwood is an exciting milestone, we have therefore created a structured transition programme that ensures every child and family feels welcome and ready to learn.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Green Oaks Federation - Partnership with Parents
pageCache.text:
Partnership with Parents
At Green Oaks, we have a strong partnership with parents and families.
We have regular opportunities for you to come into school, attend assemblies, learn about our curriculum and take part in our school life.
Year Group Information Evening
This takes place in the Autumn Term and is an opportunity to find out about the teaching and learning that your child will be part of and how you can support your child at school and home.
Curriculum Information Evening
In the Spring Term, we invite parents into school to learn more about the curriculum. Each year we focus on a different subject and explain how this is taught at school and what you can do to help at home. You then have the opportunity to see what this looks like in practice by attending one of our Shared Learning events.
Bookable Consultations
Autumn Term - Meet Your Teacher: An opportunity to talk to your child’s teacher about how they have settled into school. The teacher will also share with you your child’s baseline assessments in the different areas of learning.
Spring Term - Parent Consultations: An opportunity to meet with your child’s teacher and discuss their progress at school and learn about their next steps in learning.
In Key Stage 1 and 2 we encourage children to attend these consultations alongside their parents. This allows teachers to give direct feedback and to have a richer discussion about strengths and next steps.
Year Group Productions
Each year group has the opportunity to perform to their parents each year. This maybe putting on a Harvest celebration, a spring production or taking part in our amazing Year 2 or 6 productions!
Night School
In the Spring Term we invite parents into school to take part in a lesson with their child. This may by watching the class perform a dance routine, taking part in a Mathematics lesson or finding out how we teach personal and social skills.
Workshare
In the Summer Term you are invited into school to look at your child’s work with them. This is an opportunity for you to really talk to your child about all that they have been learning at school and to see the progress that they have made over the year.

Music
Across Green Oaks, we offer a rich and inclusive music curriculum. We aim to spark a love of learning music, with all that it offers in the way of wellbeing, self-expression, teamwork and truly memorable experiences. We hope that our children will leave primary school with a thorough grounding in music which will allow them to pursue further learning in music or to enjoy it as a lifelong hobby.
At both schools, links are made with topics and seasonal events to ensure that children listen to and perform music across a broad range of genres, historical periods and cultural backgrounds, making connections and building cultural capital. Children are taught in line with the National Curriculum aims for music, focusing on four key musical concepts: performing, composing, notation and listening. The curriculum is enriched through regular workshops such as the Drumming Workshops in Y1, Young Voices in KS2, and Sing from the 'Hart' in KS1.
Click here to view our Music Development Plan Summary
At Oakwood our children learn to play the recorder in Year 2 and at Greenfields parents are able to book instrument tuition that takes place before and after school.
During your child’s time at Greenfields they will be given the opportunity to book lessons in:
Green Oaks also has its own choir that consists of children from Year 2 - 6.
Our choir meets once a week and has the opportunity to perform at local and national events. This includes performances for our local community centre for the elderly, Singing for the Mind and our village Christmas Market.

We are fortunate to be able to offer a wide range of After School Clubs that run before and after the school day.
Details of these clubs are sent home prior to the beginning of each new term, including how to register and make payment.
Autumn Term 2026/27: All clubs will run from week commencing Monday 14th September 2026 up to and including the week commencing Monday 7th December 2026. There will be no classes on the INSET day on Monday 21st September 2026 or during half term week (26/10/26-30/10/26).

Green Oaks Young Voices
Our schools have a long history of promoting and celebrating musical talent.
The Green Oaks Choir is led by staff from across the Federation and gives children from Year 2 - 6 the opportunity to sing and perform together. The choir also performs at the village festival and other community and County events.
Choir is a whole year commitment and children are invited to join choir at the start of the Autumn Term. There is no requirement to re-register your child each term.
Music Lessons
Music lessons take place after school and are available at Greenfields for Years 3 - 6. Your child will be allocated a time slot based on availability.
Keyboard, Strings, Woodwind and Brass are all provided by Hampshire Music Service and must be booked for the whole academic year. Please look out for an email in the Summer Term inviting you to register your child's interest in music lessons.
Rock and Pop Guitar and Drum Lessons
The Rock and Pop Guitar and Drum lessons are provided independently of Hampshire Music Service and lessons and payment are organised by the provider. For details of how to book your lessons please contact Rock and Pop: www.rockandpopfoundation.com
Rock Steady Band Lessons
Rock Steady provide weekly group music lessons as part of a 'Rock Band' format. Lessons take place in school and children can choose to play either vocals, electric guitar, drums, bass, or keyboards in their very own band. All instruments are provided, and no previous experience is necessary. Bookings are taken directly with Rock Steady. If you would like to find out more, please see the following link for more details: https://www.rocksteadymusicschool.com/info-for-parents
Languages
Both schools are able to offer an after school language club through external providers. These are bookable through the links above.
Please note that no snacks or additional drinks are needed if your child attends an after school club or activity and these should not be provided due to food allergy safety.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Green Oaks Federation - PE and Sport
pageCache.text:
PE and Sport
From Reception to year 6, children will experience a variety of physical opportunities within PE lessons and across other subjects, during breaktimes, clubs and through competitive opportunities in and outside of school. This breadth of physical activity and physical education supports every child to connect with their environment and develops the whole child. Our balanced programme is essential to the development of the whole child.
Our whole school RESPECT values are firmly embedded in the PE curriculum. We develop competence in a range of physical skills, continuing to concentrate on fundamental movement skills in Lower Key Stage Two and transferring these to a variety of physical activities by the end of Key Stage 2.
Their experiences will enable pupils to:
Develop competence in a range of physical skills concentrating on fundamental movement skills at Oakwood and transfer these to a variety of sport related games and activities by the end of their time at Greenfields.
In Years 1-6, children receive 2 hours of PE a week. As core skills are repeated through different sports, children will understand how their learning links across lessons, terms and year groups.
PE planning is derived from the Get Set for Education scheme and teachers personalise the units and learning for specific pupils to enable every child to access the learning successfully. Vocabulary related to PE is directly taught and children have regular opportunities to use and apply this in their learning.
In Year R teachers target the skills from the EYFS Framework and also use Development Matters and their practitioner knowledge of child development to support them in developing a bespoke curriculum whereby they support and extend children through physical challenges in the environment and interactions from adults. PE is taught explicitly by class teacher on a weekly basis who teach the children fundamental skills in balance, dance, gymnastics and multi-skills.
At Oakwood, pupils continue to fundamental movement skills. They build on their learning in dance and gymnastics and target and striking and fielding games are introduced. In Year 2 children build further on the skills introduced in Year 1, giving them time to develop greater competency, control and confidence. Athletics and net and wall games are also introduced.
Allow children to love being active
Develop their creativity and leadership skills
Year 3
At Greenfields, in Year 3, children start to apply the fundamental skills to more recognisable sports. We make use of our on-site tennis club and coaches are used to support the teaching and learning.
Sporting Fundamentals
Year 4
In Year 4, children take their learning from ball skills in Y3 and apply this to a termly unit of tag rugby and handball. The striking and fielding skills started in Y1 and developed in Y3 now progress from cricket into rounders.
Sporting Fundamentals
Year 5
In Year 5, all children have the opportunity to develop their swimming at Hart Leisure Centre, aiming to swim at least 25m. The skills introduced, for example in tag rugby and unihoc, are developed further and pathways are provided for children into local clubs.
Year 6
In Year 6, children enjoy a broad PE offer, designed to ensure all pupils enjoy different ways of being physically active together.
*Outdoor Adventurous Activity
We believe it is our role to support your child in finding the activity or sport to develop further outside of school or beyond their time at Greenfields. We offer a broad range of clubs, many run by Level 2 coaches, and provide free access to a club of their choice for any child whose family is eligible for pupil premium.
For further information, visit After School Clubs and Activities

pageCache.pageTitle: The Green Oaks Federation - Special Educational Needs & Disability
pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs and disability (SEND)
At Green Oaks, all children are valued equally, regardless of their abilities, aptitudes, interests and behaviour. Each child is entitled to a broad, balanced, relevant and differentiated curriculum, with high aspirations for progress and achievement.
We have supported children with a range of additional needs, including speech and language, cognition and learning, hearing and visual impairment, social emotional and mental health needs, physical disabilities and needs on the Autistic Spectrum.
When considering whether one of our schools is the correct setting for your child, we would always advise that you arrange a visit to look at our environment and to talk to us about your child.

Green Oaks Inclusion Lead (SENCO)
Inclusion Leaders (ID 2242)
Q: How does Green Oaks know if my child needs extra help? At Green Oaks we have Inclusion leaders who are experienced at working with teachers and talking with parents/carers about children's progress or behaviours. They also work with other professionals and previous schools to gather information. We will also use reports from external agencies such as an Educational Psychologist, Speech and Language Therapist, Physiotherapist or other professionals.
Q: What support is there to help parent with children with SEND? Please see our SEND Information Report below. Green Oaks has an open door policy and we always encourage parents/carers to talk to the class teacher with any concerns that they may have. Half termly coffee mornings are held for families to get together to share information with professionals and other families.
Q: Who should I contact for more information on SEND? Please contact the school office to arrange an appointment with a member of the Inclusion team.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Green Oaks Federation - Vision, Values and Aims
pageCache.text:
Vision, Values and Aims
Our Vision
“Great Oaks from Little Acorns Grow”
Our vision is built on our core value of respect; respect for themselves, respect for others and respect for the environment.
Our Aims
Our Values
At Green Oaks our school values underpin all that we do. They represent our beliefs on what is important to us as educators, to the children that we teach and to the school community as a whole.
Our values are embedded throughout the curriculum, our behaviours and the school environment. We teach them directly through school assemblies and our class councils, working hard to ensure that they are understood and exemplified by all.
At Green Oaks we expect all members of our community to model and uphold our values through both words and actions.
Equality
Self-Belief
Perseverance
Excellence
Team Work and Collaboration
Respect
At Green Oaks we believe that we should respect ourselves, each other and our environment. At school we learn with each other and from each other, accepting and respecting our differences. We listen to what each other say and respect our different ideas and opinions. We show courtesy and politeness to each other and our community.
Equality
As friends we understand one another and treat each other as equals irrespective of gender, religion, ethnicity, culture or disability. We should be able to talk about our beliefs, say how we feel and make mistakes without fear of judgement or prejudice. At Green Oaks we believe that we should value and respect our similarities and differences and teach our children to understand what it means to be part of a community.
Self-Belief
At Green Oaks we want you to feel good about yourself, be proud of your achievements and believe that you can always improve through effort and hard-work. We should have the confidence to take risks, embrace challenge and the self-assurance to solve problems and achieve our goals.
Perseverance
Learning and life are not always easy and require us to learn from our successes and also from our failures. At Green Oaks we teach children how to persevere and show resilience even when things are hard. We celebrate effort and encourage our children to support and encourage each other to persevere and take pride in all that they achieve through hard work and determination.
Excellence
At Green Oaks we believe in giving our best in all that we do. Every day we learn with and from each other, and work hard to question, investigate and acquire knowledge. We believe in a Growth Mindset and are committed to excellence and instilling the confidence to persevere without fear of failure.
Creativity
At Green Oaks we believe that everyone should be given the opportunity to learn in a creative environment that inspires you to imagine, explore ideas and concepts, make connections and think critically. Creativity of thought is encouraged and children and adults are able to explore their thinking and learning with confidence and intellect.
Team Work and Collaboration
We believe that people achieve more through collaboration. We, therefore, understand what it means to be part of a team and work together to inspire learning and achieve great things. We work as a team to be part of our wider community.
We aspire to high standards for all our children, and aim to provide an inspirational, global curriculum that motivates children to learn and give their best. We aim to give all our children a positive start to school and a firm foundation for learning for the rest of their lives.
At Green Oaks we give our best and aim for excellence in all that we do.

Parents Guide To Using Our Administrative Platforms
Arbor Management Information System is the secure online platform our school uses to manage and organise important pupil information. It helps us keep accurate records of attendance, contact details, medical information, assessment data, and much more - all in one place.
Using Arbor allows staff to work more efficiently and communicate effectively with families. Parents can access the Arbor Parent Portal or app to update contact details, view attendance, book parents evening and provide various consents.
By using Arbor, we ensure that your child’s information is kept safe, up to date, and that communication between home and school is clear and consistent.
Parent's can log in to Arbor using the email address that we hold on record.
Scopay is our school’s secure online payment system. It allows parents and carers to easily pay for things like school meals, trips and clubs without needing to send cash or cheques into school.
Through the Scopay website or app, you can view your child’s balance, top up their account, and see what payments have been made. It’s quick, convenient, and helps us reduce the amount of cash handled in school.
Using Scopay makes managing payments simpler for families and ensures funds are recorded safely and accurately.
You will be issued with a Scopay access letter when your child first starts at Oakwood, and then again when they start at Greenfields.
Our school uses Google Workspace for Education to support teaching, learning, and communication. This includes tools like Google Classroom, Docs, Slides, and Drive, which allow pupils to complete work online, collaborate with classmates, and receive feedback from teachers.
These tools help make learning interactive and accessible while keeping pupils’ information safe and secure within our school’s Google domain. Each pupil is issued with their own login and password for use on the school Chromebooks.
Parental consent is required for all children to use Google Workspace for Education.
Click here to read the Google Workspace for Education information and FAQ's.
Seesaw is an online learning platform that helps children share their work and learning with teachers and families. Pupils can upload photos, videos, drawings, and assignments to their personal learning journal, giving parents a window into what they’re doing at school.
Teachers use Seesaw to set activities, give feedback, and celebrate progress, while parents can view and comment on their child’s work through the Seesaw website or app. It’s a simple and engaging way to connect home and school learning.
You will be issued with a Seesaw access letter at the start of each new academic year.
Spelling Shed is an online program that helps children learn and practise their spellings in a fun and interactive way. Through games and challenges, pupils can test themselves on word lists set by their teacher and earn points as they improve.
Children at Greenfields can use Spelling Shed at school or at home to build their confidence and accuracy with spelling, while teachers can track progress and celebrate achievements. It makes spelling practice enjoyable and motivating for every learner!
You will be issued with a Spelling Shed access letter at the start of each new academic year.
MyMaths is an online learning platform that helps children practise and develop their maths skills through interactive lessons, activities, and games. Children at Greenfields use MyMaths to complete maths tasks at home, gaining instant feedback to help them understand and improve.
It’s a fun and engaging way for pupils to build confidence in maths, while allowing teachers and parents to see how they’re progressing.
You will be issued with a MyMaths access letter at the start of each new academic year.
Times Tables Rock Stars is an online maths program designed to help children learn and recall their times tables quickly and confidently. Children at Green Oaks access TTRS at home and school to take part in fun games and friendly competition to earn coins and improve their '"rock status" whilst practising their multiplication and division facts.
Teachers can set specific times tables for pupils to focus on. It makes times tables practice exciting, motivating, and rewarding!
Student access information will be provided when your child is set up on the platform.
At school, we use the Letter-join handwriting programme to support children in developing clear, fluent, and confident handwriting. Letter-join teaches correct letter formation and joins through structured, progressive activities that help build fine motor skills and writing stamina. The programme is consistent across year groups, ensuring children develop good handwriting habits that support their wider learning.
At home access information will be provided when your child is set up on the platform.

Computing
At Green Oaks our aim is to provide an aspirational and innovative Computing Education which will equip our pupils to harness technology in a safe, purposeful and creative way. Alongside progression in knowledge, skills and understanding, we also aim for children to be inspired by computing and new learning; to be independent in the application of their knowledge and skills; and be confident in using technology to enhance the learning of other subjects.
We follow the National Centre for Computing Education (NCCE) Teach Computing curriculum which aims to transform the way that computing is taught in schools to ensure that our children are secure in a range of skills. Each year group study modules that span Computer Science, Digital Literacy and Information Technology. The NCCE is designed by experts in the computing field and teachers to ensure that lessons have clear progression and provide children with a range of knowledge and skills.
We also ensure that online safety is taught explicitly as well as being embedded into all of their lessons and assemblies. From Reception to Y6 we use Project Evolve to stimulate discussions and reflections about what it is like to be online. Children learn to take responsibility for their self-image and identity, their privacy and security, and how to manage their online reputation. During these dedicated lessons, children will also discuss the risks around online bullying and will reflect on their own digital habits and health.
In EYFS children have the opportunity to use technology as part of their continuous provision, and through this they are introduced to how to use a computer safely and responsibly.
When computing is not timetabled, children apply learning from their computing curriculum in other real-life and relevant contexts, deepening their learning and embedding core skills.
To enhance our computing curriculum, we run an annual coding club after school. If you are interested to find out more about this, please contact the school office.

pageCache.pageTitle: The Green Oaks Federation - Trips, Visits & Residentials
pageCache.text:
Trips, Visits & Residentials
All children are invited to take part in school trips and activities to widen their educational experiences and provide lasting memories.
At Oakwood, trips and visits start in Reception such day visits to Bucklebury Farm and in Years 1 and 2, other trips and visits might include Milestones Museum or The Look Out in Bracknell. The children also enjoy a wide range of visitors who come into school, for example; drumming workshops, portals from the past, and speakers from different religions.
At Greenfields, children enjoy an impressive range of trips and residential experiences. In years 3 and 4 many of the trips are closely related to specific subjects such as the visit to Butser Farm that supports their learning of the Stone Age and the trip to the Ufton Court in Year 4 that links with their learning on Anglo-Saxons.
Year 4 residential visit
When children are in Y4, they have the opportunity to participate in an overnight residential at the Gordon Brown Centre where they can take part in climbing, orienteering and camping. The children camp in group and for many, this can be their first night away from home.
Year 6 residential visit
In Upper Key Stage 2 children have the opportunity to attend another residential visit for up to a week. This allows them to take part in an even wider range of activities that are designed to build their resilience, confidence and collaboration.

History
The aim of history teaching at Green Oaks Federation is to encourage children to take an interest in the past and to understand how the world has changed and developed. History helps children to understand different societies and how the past has influenced life today in the UK and across the world.​
In EYFS (Reception), children are taught about history within the ‘Understanding the World’ area of learning. In Reception, children will begin to make sense of their own life-story and family’s history, and recognise similarities and differences between the past and the present. They will build on this learning by making connections between the features of their family and other families as well as comparing and contrasting characters from stories, including figures from the past. This strand supports children to make sense of the world around them and also help them to develop a wide and enriched vocabulary.​
Our History curriculum is taught through our thematic approach to learning and enables our children to develop the knowledge and understanding, skills, values and attitudes that they will need to participate fully in a globalised society and economy. We intend for them to understand the links and connections between events, people, places, cultures and environments through time at a local and global level. Our global themes of Environment & Sustainability and Identify & Diversity provide further opportunity for children to apply learning in real and relevant contexts. We aim for all children to be able to link facts about the past to the events of today and our attitudes towards the future.

pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium
We understand that with the cost of living crisis many families may be finding it difficult to pay for school lunches, trips, uniforms or clubs. If so, you may be eligible for Pupil Premium Grant funding:
At Green Oaks we carefully consider the potential barriers to achievement that may exist for these pupils and plan to remove these through intervention and support.
Our Pupil Premium Plan is reviewed each academic year and agreed by our School Governing Body.
To check your eligibility, please visit and apply online.
After making an application, If you are eligible the school will be notified directly and will contact you. If you have any questions regarding pupil Premium eligibility, please contact the School Office.
Use of Pupil Premium at Green Oaks Federation
At Green Oaks Federation, we have high expectations for all our pupils and work hard to ensure that all pupils make good progress across the school and achieve their best. Each pupil’s progress is evaluated at three milestones over the course of the year through Pupil Progress Meetings and additional support is provided for any pupils at risk of not making good progress.
Our Pupil Premium Lead and Assistant Headteacher at Greenfields, Mrs Magowan, has particular responsibility for ensuring that there is high-quality provision for children receiving Free School Meals or who are Looked After at both schools. Mrs Magowan meets with the designated Pupil Premium Governor once a term.
Pupil Premium Lead closely monitors and evaluates the academic progress, attendance and attainment of each Pupil Premium child and the associated groups.
Our Inclusion Leader takes on the role of Designated Teacher for our Looked after and Post looked after children at each school. The Pupil Premium Lead liaises with the Inclusion Leader regarding the provisions and funding in place.
